title: Integral closure of an affine torsion-free monoid algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $P$ a fine commutative monoid, written additively [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], such that $G=P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ is torsion free. Put $P^{\mathrm{sat}}=\{g\in G:ng\in P\text{ for some integer }n>0\}$. For a submonoid $Q\subseteq G$ write $k[Q]=\bigoplus_{q\in Q}ke^q$, with multiplication $e^qe^{q'}=e^{q+q'}$. The natural maps embed $k[P]\subseteq k[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]\subseteq k[G]$, all three rings are integral domains, and they have the same fraction field $K=\operatorname{Frac}(k[G])$. Inside $K$, $k[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ is the integral closure of $k[P]$: it is exactly the set of elements of $K$ satisfying a monic polynomial with coefficients in $k[P]$. Moreover $k[P^{\mathrm{sat}}]$ is a finite $k[P]$-module and is integrally closed in $K$. The zero-rank case $P=G=\{0\}$ and monoids with nontrivial units are allowed.
